examples.name: Basic entity tagging
examples.description: Hold the node array, resolve queries from your own data, and give each entity type a tone. Typing `/` opens the picker.

examples.name: Recents on open
examples.description: Supply `recents` so opening the picker is instant - `onSearch` is then only called once a query is typed.

examples.name: Tone and icon per entity type
examples.description: entityConfig drives both the picker's section heading tile and the inserted tag, so color encodes type consistently in both places.

props.entityConfig: { person: blue + PersonIcon, matter: teal + FolderIcon, roadmap: purple + RoadmapIcon }

examples.name: Prefilled from stored content
examples.description: Hydrate from a saved node array. The editor reads it on mount and leads from then on - onChange reports every later edit.

examples.name: People rows with avatars
examples.description: A row leading with an Avatar or AvatarGroup renders inline and hugs its width, with no description line - matching Figma's People and Families lists.

examples.name: Sizes, context and states
examples.description: The frame axes are Text Area's, unchanged: sm/md/lg sizes and the default/inline context. The deprecated `appearance` still works (subtle and inline map to context="inline").
examples.jsx:
<RichTextArea size="lg" aria-label="Large" value={a} onChange={setA} onSearch={search} />
<RichTextArea context="inline" aria-label="Inline" value={b} onChange={setB} onSearch={search} />
<RichTextArea invalid aria-label="Invalid" value={c} onChange={setC} onSearch={search} />
<RichTextArea disabled aria-label="Disabled" value={d} onChange={setD} onSearch={search} />

examples.name: Labelled by Field
examples.description: Field names the editor by aria-labelledby (a label's htmlFor can't name a div) and passes its message, error, and required, which the editor sets as aria-describedby, aria-invalid, and aria-required.
examples.jsx:
<Field label="Notes" message="Type / to link a matter" state="error" required>
  <RichTextArea value={value} onChange={setValue} onSearch={search} />
</Field>

antiExamples.name: Using it for plain multi-line text
antiExamples.reason: With nothing to link to, this is a contenteditable div standing in for a <textarea> - losing native keyboard, autofill, spellcheck and scrolling behavior for no benefit. Use TextArea.

antiExamples.name: Driving the value on every keystroke
antiExamples.reason: The editor hydrates from `value` once and then leads. Re-rendering a contenteditable surface from props on each keystroke would destroy the caret, so later `value` changes are deliberately ignored - treat it as initial content, not a live binding.

antiExamples.name: Storing the value as HTML
antiExamples.reason: The node array is the stable contract. Round-tripping through HTML leaks the editor's DOM shape into your data and forces every consumer to parse it back out - persist the nodes, or map them to your own shape.

antiExamples.name: The same tone for every entity type
antiExamples.jsx:
<RichTextArea
  aria-label="Note"
  value={value}
  onChange={setValue}
  onSearch={search}
  entityConfig={{
    account: { tone: 'default', icon: <TeamAndPartnersIcon decorative /> },
    matter: { tone: 'default', icon: <FolderIcon decorative /> },
  }}
/>
antiExamples.reason: With one tone for every type, people can't tell a person from a matter at a glance. Give each entityType its own tone, so a tag's color says what it links to.

antiExamples.name: Clearing the note by passing a new value
antiExamples.jsx:
<RichTextArea value={note} onChange={setNote} onSearch={search} aria-label="Note" />

// Later. The editor still shows the old text.
setNote([]);
antiExamples.reason: The editor reads value only when it mounts, so a new value passed later - including an empty array to clear it - is ignored and the old text stays on screen.
